newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC okays New England power pool's ISO plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC okays New England power pool's ISO plan.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday conditionally approved a plan by the New England Power Pool to set up an independent system operator to run transmission and other services for the group.

The FERC approved the member utilities' plan to hand over control of their transmission facilities to the ISO, whose role will be to run the system reliably as more power producers and marketers enter the market, administer the pool's tariff, and oversee the NEPOOL power exchange.
The commission imposed four conditions on the approval, which it expected the power pool to meet easily.

To ensure that the ISO board was truly independent of NEPOOL utilities, the group would have to lower the threshold for defining a utility "affiliate" on the board to include any company 10 percent owned by a utility, instead of 50 percent-owned. The board would only be allowed to have a certain number of utility affiliates.
NEPOOL utility employees who become board members of the ISO would have to divest any financial interests they might have in their former employers.
The ISO would have to become self-funding, a condition which NEPOOL said it would meet by charging transaction fees.
And NEPOOL membership would have to be opened to utilities outside New England.
The commission said it would review the power pool's open access tariff and pricing policies later.
